{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the bottom tail (stroke 4) and laid it from the belly line out to the right edge, about 23 dominoes across five build runs. Omar confirmed it took the fall from the belly and went dark all the way round. That gave the fish its lower tail curve and a good share of the falling outline.

Execution: I picked one piece of work and finished it quietly. I traced stroke 4 as drawn on the pad and kept it connected to the belly line. After that I inspected the tail edge several times and passed Omar a specific observation: the last dark domino on the belly side pointed up, and the next one sat slightly off its path, so it needed nudging into line. That was a precise diagnosis he could act on straight away.

Collaboration: I kept clear of Omar and Sofia while they worked near the tail edge so we wouldn't bump each other's dominoes. I offered to take the top of the tail so Omar could hold the bridge, and I told him to shout if he wanted a hand. I acknowledged the team's work at the end and followed the hands-off call before the push.

Leadership: I led by example. I took the piece assigned to me without being chased, finished it, and then used my free hands to check and advise instead of adding clutter. When the group agreed to stop touching the tail, I backed that call, which kept the standing picture intact for the push.", "my_share_percent": 25}
